commits.author: giuliastro
commits.subject: feat(launcher): auto-start the machine daemon on multi-agent hosts (#158)
commits.body:
A machine with several agents installed was the one case the one-command path
refused to handle: it detected them and exited asking for --backend. It now
starts the machine daemon instead, selecting an ACP primary from a documented
order, printing it, and including managed OpenCode when installed.

`--backend` selects the daemon primary, matching what the same flag means to the
daemon itself, and `--single` is the explicit opt-out to the legacy path. The
launcher assigns managed OpenCode a free loopback port, excluding its own, so an
OpenCode already listening on 4096 degrades to a different port rather than
aborting the zero-config launch it was meant to enable.

The launch plan is a pure function of the detected list, so the decision is
tested directly rather than through a spawned process.

commits.author: giuliastro
commits.subject: fix(tests): compare project paths against canonical temporary roots (#165)
commits.body:
`main` had been red since #159. The desktop workflow runs the bridge suite on
macOS and Windows as well as Linux, and one project-catalog test failed on both
of the first two: it asserted that a discovered project's path equalled the
value `mkdtemp` returned, while the catalog reports the canonical path.

The temporary directory is not canonical outside Linux. macOS returns
`/var/folders/...`, a symlink to `/private/var/folders/...`; Windows returns the
8.3 alias `C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...` of `C:\Users\runneradmin\...`. The assertion
was therefore checking the platform's alias rather than the behaviour under
test, and only Linux — where `/tmp` happens to be real — agreed with it.

The source is right to canonicalize: a project id must not change with the route
taken to the root, and the root-boundary check has to compare resolved paths.
So the test moves to the canonical root, through one helper the whole file uses.

Pull-request checks only ran the bridge suite on Linux, so this class of failure
could not be seen until after the merge. They now run it on macOS and Windows
too — the bridge has no dependencies, so the extra runners cost a checkout and
`node --test`.

+- **Task-first client UX** — expose the existing project/task/worktree/launch primitives as the normal way to create work from phone, web and desktop.

-- **Worktree isolation** — concurrent tasks get isolated Git workspaces rather than colliding in one checkout.
-- **Finish-work loop** — diff → tests → review → PR as a first-class workflow.
-- **Multi-machine fleet** — supervise and eventually route work across desktops, laptops and servers without moving credentials or repositories into a hosted control plane.
